parts.note: read as a ground where trains are sorted and assembled into order, rather than a place for exercise or drill

explanation.definitionFit: A railway sidings area where wagons are sorted and made up into trains is literally ground for forming trains.

parts.note: read not as bad company but as a crowd made of wrongs, a great host of misdeeds

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical phrase (charity covers a great many) describes a vast number of sinful acts, a crowd of wrongdoings.

parts.note: to study a subject at university is to read it

explanation.surface: An instruction to study an English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade is a nineteenth-century English novelist, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Captive man on his own has to do some gardening outside

indicators.note: the gardening word is placed on the outside, wrapping round the man on his own

parts.note: to hoe is to do some gardening, breaking up soil and weeds
a stag is a man attending a function unaccompanied by a woman

explanation.surface: A lone man is told he must do some weeding out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like it says where the gardening is done; it is the container signal. A stag is a man going to a party unaccompanied.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive as security for demands.

clue.text: Drip's intentional disclosure of secret information

definitions.meaning: a drip is a slow escape of liquid through a hole
a deliberate release of confidential material to the press

explanation.surface: A dull person's deliberate leaking of classified secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a slow seepage of fluid and the deliberate passing of secrets to outsiders.

clue.text: Fluid, sometimes invisible, we will get in this reservoir

parts.note: ink is a writing fluid, and spies' ink can be invisible
contracted to we'll, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: We can pour a fluid that is sometimes invisible into this container.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkwell is a small pot holding a supply of writing fluid, a little reservoir.

clue.text: Pin fastening the piston to a fish?

definitions.meaning: the pin joining a piston to its connecting rod in an engine
a small freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A query whether an engine's piston pin might be a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names an engineering pin linking piston and rod and a small European freshwater fish.

indicators.note: a recipe is a way of mixing ingredients, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An exclamation of devotion to a recipe for tandoori food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe' looks like the thing being worshipped, but it is the mixing signal, working on 'tandoori' alone; the A is given as it is at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep reverence and love, the attitude of worship.

parts.note: profoundly hints at depth; a person in these places is at the very bottom of hopelessness

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the lowest point of hopelessness, where someone is most deeply dejected.

clue.text: Two pages to track down on celery, say

parts.note: a leaf of a book has two pages, one on each side
to stalk is to follow and track down prey

explanation.surface: Two pages of instructions on hunting down celery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks celery as an example: the edible part of celery is a leafstalk.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery's edible part is the petiole, the stem that bears a leaf, so celery exemplifies one.

clue.text: Daughter not well coming back for flag

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

indicators.note: the word for not well is read backwards, as if returning

parts.note: poor health means not being well

explanation.surface: A sick daughter returns home for a flag-day event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' reverses POOR to ROOP. 'flag' looks like a banner, but here it is the verb meaning to wilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire and wilt, to sag or hang down limply.

definitions.meaning: a lotion for bathing sore eyes

explanation.surface: A claim that a remedy for eyes is worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a lotion for bathing the eyes and nonsense or humbug.

indicators.note: turned means the word for limb is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: A limb that has turned into wobbly jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A gel is a jelly-like substance, a colloid set firm.

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shriek as the singer Lulu performs on guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer; 'playing' rearranges EEK and LULU.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukulele is a small four-stringed instrument of the guitar family from Hawaii.

clue.text: Do not fully appreciate the lower speed

parts.note: under means lower, beneath
rate means speed, as in rate of knots

explanation.surface: Failing to value properly how slow something is going.
explanation.definitionFit: To underrate is to undervalue, rating something below its worth.

parts.note: le is French for the
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking for a French version of a garland.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian wreath of flowers worn round the neck.

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their normal order

explanation.surface: Someone spots a lion and shouts at it to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get out' reads as a shout, but 'get' is fodder and 'out' alone rearranges LION and GET.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentigo is a medical term for small brown skin spots such as freckles.

clue.text: The queen and the king make a mistake

parts.note: ER, Elizabetha Regina, is the queen's royal cipher
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A royal couple both getting something wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to be wrong, to slip up.

parts.note: complaint is a disease, not a grumble, one confined to a particular area or people

explanation.definitionFit: An endemic is a disease regularly found in a particular region.

clue.text: Place where security device was found underneath the carpet

indicators.note: underneath puts the device below the carpet in this down entry

parts.note: a mat is a small carpet
a lock secures doors

explanation.surface: A key safety mechanism discovered hidden beneath the rug.
explanation.walkthrough: Matlock is a town in Derbyshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Matlock is the county town of Derbyshire, a named location.

parts.note: caps are covers or lids
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Brown lids on a turning spindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a rotating vertical drum used on ships for winding cable.

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
had means possessed or owned

explanation.surface: Dad showed he was unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown is to scowl, showing disapproval with the brow.

clue.text: Word of warning was arranged, was aware beforehand

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout warning of a ball in flight

indicators.note: arranged means the following word's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A warning was set up, as someone had anticipated.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is a golfer's warning shout; 'arranged' turns WAS into SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to know in advance, to anticipate.

clue.text: Lock-opening tool used in joust, it is found within

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the words joust, it is, running across them

explanation.surface: A lockpick used in a medieval tournament, discovered inside.
explanation.walkthrough: An oustiti is a burglar's tool for turning a key from the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An oustiti is a pincer-like tool for gripping a key from the far side of a door, to open a lock.

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them

explanation.surface: A swindler is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss and trouble, bother.

indicators.note: reportedly means the number is as heard spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: four is a number
top means highest

explanation.surface: A figure, so it is said, standing on the topmost stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretop is a platform at the top of a ship's foremast.

indicators.note: included means the second piece is put inside the first

parts.note: rests are remainders or balances
one is gives I'S, read as IS

explanation.surface: Someone resists the inclusion of their own share of accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is I + S (one is), placed inside RESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or withstand.

clue.text: Play legato quietly or drink noisily

parts.note: to slur notes is to play them smoothly joined, legato
p, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A musical choice between playing smoothly and softly, or gulping a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To slurp is to drink with a loud sucking sound.

clue.text: I am past the mature stage

parts.note: contracted to I'm, written without the apostrophe
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are beyond adulthood.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final adult form of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Teresa takes it with over half the range, ordinary range of pitch

parts.note: Tess is a short form of the name Teresa

indicators.note: over, read with half, asks for more than half of the range's name, so its last letter goes and three of four stay

parts.note: the range is the Urals, a Russian mountain chain; 'half' joins 'over' to ask for more than half of it

explanation.surface: Teresa takes most of the scale, singing within her usual compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over half' means more than half: three of the four letters of URAL (the Ural mountains) stay. 'takes' and 'with' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessitura is the range within which most notes of a vocal part lie, a singer's usual compass.

clue.text: Have something to say under one's breath

definitions.text: Have something to say under one's breath

parts.words: Have something to say under one's breath
parts.note: to say something quietly so others can barely hear, murmuring softly

explanation.definitionFit: Murmuring very softly is uttering words quietly without full voice.
